**Uke 19.–25. juli — Sunday Review**

**Shift Impact**
Re-entry week did exactly what quick-returns do. The Tue evening → Wed day transition is visible as a cliff: bed 02:16 before a 07:30 start, then 6h20 → 6h02 → 4h21 across the three day shifts. Readiness went 75 → 47 → 57 → 17 over the same span. Nothing surprising here — the roster forced it, and Saturday's 11-hour recovery sleep (wake 15:05) was the predictable payback. Noted, not moralized.

**Training**
Two things. The Jul 20 run is the already-flagged session — 83% Z4, 13% Z5, avg HR 167, sprint-y fastest 1k of 6:36 — same signature as May/June. It also happened during the running hold, so the ladder logic and the actual behavior diverged this week. Good that Achilles work is happening off-log, but unlogged rehab means I can't see rung progression, only the violations. Second: the Jul 24 walk (avg HR 126, 25% Z3, +147m climb) on readiness 17 wasn't nothing — that's aerobic-base load on a POOR day. Fine as a one-off, worth noticing as a pattern.

**Nutrition**
This is the section that needs pushback. Logged days averaged ~2,060 kcal against a 1,600 target, with two outright surplus days (Jul 21: 2,646 in vs 2,454 burn; Jul 25: 2,608 vs 2,219). The deficit didn't get masked this week — it didn't exist. And the composition shifted: sugar hit 172g, 133g, and 186g on three days while fiber cratered to 1.9g and 5.5g. Protein swung 84–135g. This isn't glycogen noise territory; it's a genuine off-week, likely riding the vacation tail plus sleep-deprived days (short sleep → sugar cravings is a real mechanism, and the worst sugar days line up with the worst sleep).

**Recovery**
HRV 79 → 66 across the week, RHR up 3, sleep score down 13. All consistent with the quick-return block plus the intake pattern — no red flags beyond what the roster explains, and everything stayed BALANCED. ACWR sitting at 0.5–0.6 means chronic load is decaying; expected during the running hold, but it means the eventual return-to-run needs to be gentler than instinct will suggest.

**Body Composition / Trend**
Worth its slot this week: 78.5kg on Jul 20 vs the ~76.6 June baseline is ~2kg up, and unlike previous stalls, this one has a matching intake story. The 27.4% BF reading on Jul 24 is probably inflated (water 53%, post-short-sleep), so don't read that number literally — but the weight direction is real.

**Key Takeaway**
The week's story is one thing: the deficit was off, not hidden. Re-entry weeks get grace, so no adherence flogging — but next week's single job is getting logged intake back near 1,600 with sugar under control, because the 2kg drift is now signal, not water. Everything else (Achilles ladder, Z2 discipline, Day B) resumes from there.

Shift Impact — N/A (this is the point)
Zero shifts this week — full vacation, the no-shift baseline test for the sleep drift question. Verdict: drift persisted without shift pressure. Bedtimes went 01:44 → 22:51 → 03:22 → 02:58 → 03:25 → 04:48 → 01:29. That's not shift-confounded circadian delay, and it's not "recovering from work" either — it got progressively worse as the week went on with nothing external forcing it. This points more toward the psychological pull (evening time feels more valuable) than the light/circadian explanation, since a pure light effect wouldn't have gotten worse day 5-6 into a rest week. Worth locking in the soft ceiling (~00:30) as the next move rather than waiting for more data — you have your answer.
Training — basically a rest week
One real session all week: July 2's mixed walk/run block. The run segment (1.74km) landed 47% Z3 / 48% Z4 with an elevation gain of 65m in under 2km — that's a steep short segment, and it's the same pattern as before: terrain overrides Z2 intent immediately. Load is dropping fast (297→168 over the week, ACWR 1.2→0.6), which is fine and expected for a deliberate rest week, but it does mean you're bleeding some training effect if this stretches longer. Steps cratered too — 325 on July 2, sub-2,500 average for the week. This is recovery-week territory, not a Z2-habit-building week, so don't read anything into the Z2 failure here beyond "same structural issue, small sample."
